shipping.sub: How orders leave our factory, and why made-to-specification abrasives are not returnable.
shipping.shipSub: Production, packing and dispatch are confirmed together with your quotation.
shipping.s1b: Abrasive belts, discs and flap discs are converted to the specification in your order. Lead time starts from the date the quotation is confirmed in writing, not from the date the enquiry was sent. Standard references such as GXK-51, XZ-330 and GPC71 are ready-made stock items; custom sizes, grits and OEM packaging are made to order.
shipping.s2b: Goods are packed in export cartons with the agreed pack quantity, labels, carton marks and — for OEM programmes — your artwork and barcode. Pallet configuration is confirmed with the packing list. Fumigation or ISPM 15 markings are applied where the destination country requires them.
shipping.s3b: Shipment is arranged by sea (FCL or LCL) or air, depending on volume and destination. The trade term is stated on your quotation — EXW, FOB, CIF, CFR, DAP and DDP are commonly used. You may nominate your own forwarder; MoTai then supplies the packing list, carton marks and shipping documents.
shipping.s4b: Each shipment is accompanied by a commercial invoice, packing list and transport document. HS codes and certificates of origin are provided for your customs clearance. Import duties, taxes and customs clearance in the destination country are for the buyer's account unless the quotation states DDP.
shipping.s5b: We send the shipping advice with the vessel or flight number once the container or consignment is booked. Delivery time depends on the destination port or airport and the carrier's schedule. Delays caused by port congestion, customs inspection or force majeure are outside our control and are notified as soon as they are known.
shipping.retSub: Our products are made to the agreed specification, which is why returns are limited to defined cases.
shipping.r1b: Abrasive products are manufactured to your grit, size, backing and packaging specification. Because they cannot be resold as standard stock, confirmed custom orders are not returnable and are not refundable, except where the goods do not match the confirmed specification.
shipping.r2b: Standard reference items that have not been used and remain in their original export packing can be returned on a case-by-case basis after we confirm the reason and the return conditions. Goods damaged in transit must be reported with photographs within 7 days of delivery, and claims on the carrier's insurance are handled through the named forwarder.
shipping.r3b: Any claim must reference the order number, the packing list and the affected carton marks. Where a defect is confirmed after inspection, we either replace the affected quantity or issue a credit note against the invoice. Claims raised more than 30 days after delivery cannot be accepted.
shipping.r4b: Where a credit is agreed, any refund is made to the original payer by the same method used for the order, once the return or replacement has been completed or written off. Bank charges on international transfers are borne by the party receiving the refund.
shipping.r5b: Returns requested because of import restrictions, duties, customs inspection or local compliance rules are treated as commercial disputes rather than product claims, because the goods were delivered in accordance with the confirmed specification.
shipping.related: Shipping and returns terms form part of every quotation. If a quotation states different terms, that quotation prevails.

order.q: Does requesting a quote place an order?
order.a: No. The form starts a wholesale enquiry. Product specifications, availability and commercial terms are confirmed before an order is agreed.

sample.q: Can I test a sample before committing to a full order?
sample.a: Yes. Samples of standard references are available for evaluation on request; sample availability and freight terms are confirmed with your quotation.

lead.q: How far ahead should I place a production order?
lead.a: Lead time starts from the date the quotation is confirmed in writing and depends on the size, grit and packaging ordered. Stock references ship fastest.

beltSize.q: Can abrasive belts be supplied in a non-standard size or length?
beltSize.a: Belt width and length beyond the documented sizes are quoted case by case; converting to a custom size affects both lead time and minimum order quantity.

beltJoint.q: What belt joint and edge construction do these belts use?
beltJoint.a: Joint type and edge treatment are specified per reference. State the machine, load and finish required so the right construction is priced in your quotation.

discBacking.q: How do I choose between hook & loop, PSA and mesh discs?
discBacking.a: Hook & loop suits frequent grit changes, PSA suits flat pads and long run times, and mesh discs suit dust extraction. Our selection guide compares the three side by side.

discDust.q: Are these discs compatible with dust extraction?
discDust.a: Mesh and perforated discs are designed for extraction; solid discs can be supplied perforated on request. State your extraction setup and the pad you are running.

hookLoop.q: Will hook & loop discs fit my existing backup pad?
hookLoop.a: Diameter and hole pattern must match the pad. Confirm your sander model and pad diameter with the enquiry so the right disc is quoted.

psa.q: Do PSA discs work with any backup pad?
psa.a: PSA discs need a flat, clean rubber pad of the matching diameter. Confirm pad diameter and machine model with your quotation request.

mesh.q: How long does a mesh abrasive disc last?
mesh.a: Mesh discs resist loading in dust-heavy work, which usually extends useful life compared with solid paper discs. Actual life depends on material, pressure and grit.

solid.q: Can solid discs be supplied perforated for dust extraction?
solid.a: Yes — perforation pattern is agreed with the quotation. State the pad and extraction setup so the correct pattern is quoted.

alum.def: The most common abrasive grain for belts and discs: tough, workable, suited to metal, wood and general finishing.

ansi.def: Legacy North American grit numbering. Similar-size grains differ from the FEPA scale — name the standard in every enquiry.

backing-cloth.def: A cotton/cloth web that carries the abrasive grain on belts. Weight (e.g. X-weight) sets flexibility and load capacity.

backing-poly.def: Poly-cotton web backing: a balance of strength and flexibility for general-purpose belts.

belt.def: A continuous loop of abrasive grain on a web backing, used on belt machines for grinding, finishing and deburring.

blend.def: Smoothing a weld so it blends into the surrounding metal — typically a first pass on a flap disc or belt, then finer grits.

closed.def: A close-coated grain layout with little open space; the belt resists clogging on harder work.

debur.def: Removing burrs and small protrusions left by cutting, sawing or grinding.

dust.def: Removing abrasive dust at the workpiece — via pad ports, open-mesh discs or local extraction.

flap.def: A disc of overlapping abrasive flaps, flexible, for grinding, blending and finishing on angle grinders.

fepa.def: The ISO 848 (FEPA) grading scale in P-notation (e.g. P120). The default scale in most European and international trade.

grit.def: The nominal grain size of an abrasive: higher numbers are finer. Belts 40–800; discs 60–5000.

hookloop.def: The hook-and-loop attachment system for discs: the disc snaps onto a hook-faced pad.

mesh.def: Open-mesh discs have cut-out windows for dust to pass through, needing a compatible pad and extraction.

moq.def: Minimum order quantity — comes with the offer, alongside availability and terms.

oem.def: Original equipment manufacturing / private label: our products under your brand, labels and packaging.

psa.def: Pressure-sensitive adhesive backing: the disc sticks directly onto a compatible pad.

disc.def: A flat or flapped abrasive circle mounted on a pad for sanding and finishing.

sic.def: Silicon carbide grain: very hard, sharp, suited to glass, ceramics and non-ferrous metals.

prep.def: Getting a surface ready for coating or finishing: removing rust, filler or old finish to a consistent profile.

wetdry.def: Grades that stay cool and clog-resistant in wet or wet/dry use; confirm suitability with the quotation.

xweight.def: A mid-weight cloth backing for general-purpose belts: strong yet flexible.

zirconia.def: Zirconia alumina grain: tough and aggressive for metal grinding, deburring and finishing on steel.

pad.def: The backing plate a disc sits on: pad diameter, face (hook) and port layout must match the disc.
